discharged pus for the previous 10 months without any trauma to her head
denied any symptoms, including fever

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of a swelling on the right upper eyelid discharging pus, combined with imaging findings of a high signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus, and expansion of the right frontal sinus without bone destruction, are consistent with a frontal sinus mucocele.

The patient's history of swelling and discharge from the right upper eyelid, along with imaging findings of opacification in the right frontal sinus and mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis, suggest chronic frontal sinusitis.

The patient's symptoms of a swelling on the right upper eyelid discharging pus, combined with imaging findings of a high signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus, are consistent with a frontal sinus pyocele.

The patient's symptoms of a swelling on the right upper eyelid discharging pus, combined with imaging findings of a high signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus, could be consistent with an orbital subperiosteal abscess.

The patient's symptoms of a swelling on the right upper eyelid discharging pus, combined with imaging findings of a high signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus, and expansion of the right frontal sinus without bone destruction, are consistent with a frontoethmoidal mucocele.

rationales.F02: Pus discharge suggests an infectious or inflammatory process, which is more typical of frontal sinus pyocele or chronic frontal sinusitis.
rationales.F06: The presence of a scarlike node discharging pus on the eyelid is more suggestive of frontal sinus pyocele.
rationales.F07: Ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus on MRI is highly suggestive of frontal sinus mucocele or pyocele.
rationales.F08: Opacification of the frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses is consistent with chronic frontal sinusitis or a mucocele.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of an immovable scarlike node discharging pus and the imaging findings of high signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus, along with expansion of the right frontal sinus and right ethmoid sinus without bone destruction, are more indicative of a pyocele, which is a collection of pus within a sinus, than a mucocele, which is a collection of mucus.
